key_insight: Alterbute introduces a diffusion-based editing framework with a relaxed training objective and attribute-aware conditioning that lets you change an object's intrinsic attributes (color, texture, material, even shape) while preserving its perceived identity and scene context.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between identity-preserving image edits and flexible intrinsic attribute manipulation: existing methods either fail to keep object identity (unsupervised priors) or are too constrained by supervision to produce meaningful, diverse attribute changes.
method: Diffusion-based editing backbone that operates on an object-localized region to produce high-quality intrinsic attribute changes.
Relaxed training objective that encourages meaningful attribute variation while explicitly preserving object identity and scene context via identity-aware/perceptual constraints.
Attribute-aware conditioning (e.g., masks or reference attribute signals) and latent-space manipulation to support edits of color, texture, material and shape without breaking object identity.
impact: Enables fine-grained, identity-preserving object edits useful for image retouching, controlled data augmentation, and content creation workflows, reducing reliance on heavy supervision or brittle priors.
visual_elements: Before / after image panels showing the same object with edits to color, texture, material and shape while background and identity remain constant.
Pipeline diagram: input image + object mask → diffusion editor with relaxed objective → edited image, with callouts for identity-preserving constraints and attribute conditioning.
UI mockup with attribute sliders (color, texture, material, shape) demonstrating controllable editing.
Bar/line chart comparing identity-preservation and edit-fidelity metrics against representative baselines.
paper_title: Alterbute: Editing Intrinsic Attributes of Objects in Images
paper_authors: Tal Reiss, Daniel Winter, Matan Cohen, Alex Rav-Acha, Yael Pritch
